question: What happened to noninterest expense, the efficiency (overhead) ratio and compensation expense?

answer.summary: Noninterest expense for JPMorgan Chase was $87.2 billion in FY2023, up 14% year over year [T00962]. The increase was predominantly driven by higher compensation expense, reflecting growth in employees primarily in technology and front office, as well as wage inflation [T00962]. Share-based compensation specifically rose to $3.12 billion in FY2023, an 11.6% increase from $2.79 billion in FY2022 [F03451]. The noninterest expense increase also includes the $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment and costs associated with the First Republic acquisition [T00962]. The efficiency (overhead) ratio is not in the retrieved evidence.
drivers: Higher compensation expense (employee growth in technology and front office, plus wage inflation) - the predominant driver of the 14% noninterest expense increase [T00962]
risks_and_red_flags: Efficiency ratio not disclosed in the retrieved evidence, so overhead efficiency relative to revenue cannot be assessed
14% noninterest expense growth may outpace revenue growth; revenue trend not provided in evidence to contextualize the expense increase [T00962]
Segment-level noninterest expense figures ($5.4B up 14% [T01421], $28.6B up 5% [T01362], $12.8B up 8% [T01465]) are slices of the firm, not the company total [T01421][T01362][T01465]
data_quality_notes: Efficiency (overhead) ratio is not present in the retrieved evidence; cannot report this metric
Share-based compensation is a subset of total compensation expense; total compensation figure is not separately disclosed in the evidence
Segment noninterest expense numbers are component slices and must not be summed to the company total

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 noninterest expense of $87.2 billion, up 14% YoY, with share-based compensation up 11.6% to $3.12 billion [T00962][F03451]
outlook.forward_looking_guidance: No forward-looking management guidance on noninterest expense or efficiency ratio is included in the retrieved evidence

follow_up_checks: Locate the efficiency ratio in the 10-K income statement or MD&A to assess overhead efficiency relative to revenue
Compare noninterest expense growth against revenue growth to determine if expense expansion is justified
Verify total compensation expense (not just share-based) in the compensation discussion of MD&A
Confirm whether the $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment is expected to recur in future periods
